verdict_basis: Closed by the validator's own rebuild, not by the producer's pod alone. A validator-made git archive of e9d5dbdccd (on origin/main), built with the official Rust 1.97.0 toolchain (rustc, rust-std, cargo and rustup verified file-by-file against static.rust-lang.org) and crates.io crates under Cargo.lock checksums, replays the committed session 288/288 identical; and the measured binary 8f9576b5 is instruction- and data-equivalent to that build (and to the producer pod build d012489f) apart from link layout and the CARGO_HOME prefix in panic paths. The producer pod evidence checks out in every respect tested and is consistent corroboration; on its own it would only narrow F5 (C5).

residuals: The fresh re-run (rerun-session/) exists only from the producer-orchestrated pod; it is consistent (all counted fields equal the original on 336/336 records) but the validator did not re-run the spec, so it is corroboration, not load-bearing. F5 closure rests on the validator replay (C6) and binary equivalence (C7).

C-compiled parts (bundled sqlite, blake3 C/asm) were compiled by each host's system cc, which was not verified; their machine code is identical across the original, the pod and the validator builds, and they are not in the counting path.

The validator build and replay ran on this container (env class ECBENV3hb516f42f4ab3, the original validation replay host class), not on the run host class (ECBENV3h3ea0ce3c3fe0). Counts are host-independent and replayed identically on both classes.

session.json and records still carry git_commit null / git_dirty null; the binding is now the validator rebuild equivalence recorded here, which the validation gate documents must cite (status changes are not made by this validator).
Scope: closing F5 does not change F2 (H1 unresolved inside the band), F3/F4 (no admissible wall figure) or any other open finding.
